# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/resolv-conf/latest/target-redirect/src/resolv_conf/lib.rs.html

# resolv_conf/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! The crate simply parses `/etc/resolv.conf` file and creates a config object
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! # Examples
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! ## Parsing a config from a string
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! ```rust
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! extern crate resolv_conf;
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! use std::net::{Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr};
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! use resolv_conf::{ScopedIp, Config, Network};
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! fn main() {
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!     let config_str = "
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! options ndots:8 timeout:8 attempts:8
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! domain example.com
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! search example.com sub.example.com
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! nameserver 2001:4860:4860::8888
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! nameserver 2001:4860:4860::8844
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! nameserver 8.8.8.8
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! nameserver 8.8.4.4
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! options rotate
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! options inet6 no-tld-query
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! sortlist 130.155.160.0/255.255.240.0 130.155.0.0";
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!     // Parse the config.
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!     let parsed_config = Config::parse(&config_str).expect("Failed to parse config");
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!     // We can build configs manually as well, either directly or with Config::new()
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!     let mut expected_config = Config::new();
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!     expected_config.nameservers = vec![
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!         ScopedIp::V6(Ipv6Addr::new(0x2001, 0x4860, 0x4860, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x8888), None),
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!         ScopedIp::V6(Ipv6Addr::new(0x2001, 0x4860, 0x4860, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x8844), None),
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!         ScopedIp::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(8, 8, 8, 8)),
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!         ScopedIp::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(8, 8, 4, 4)),
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!     ];
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!     expected_config.sortlist = vec![
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!         Network::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(130, 155, 160, 0), Ipv4Addr::new(255, 255, 240, 0)),
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!         Network::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(130, 155, 0, 0), Ipv4Addr::new(255, 255, 0, 0)),
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!     ];
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!     expected_config.debug = false;
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!     expected_config.ndots = 8;
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     expected_config.timeout = 8;
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!     expected_config.attempts = 8;
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!     expected_config.rotate = true;
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!     expected_config.no_check_names = false;
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!     expected_config.inet6 = true;
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!     expected_config.ip6_bytestring = false;
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!     expected_config.ip6_dotint = false;
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!     expected_config.edns0 = false;
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!     expected_config.single_request = false;
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!     expected_config.single_request_reopen = false;
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!     expected_config.no_tld_query = true;
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!     expected_config.use_vc = false;
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!     expected_config.set_domain(String::from("example.com"));
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!     expected_config.set_search(vec![
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!         String::from("example.com"),
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!         String::from("sub.example.com")
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!     ]);
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!     // We can compare configurations, since resolv_conf::Config implements Eq
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!     assert_eq!(parsed_config, expected_config);
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! }
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! ```
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! ## Parsing a file
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! ```rust
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! use std::io::Read;
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! use std::fs::File;
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! extern crate resolv_conf;
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! fn main() {
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//!     // Read the file
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!     let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(4096);
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!     let mut f = File::open("/etc/resolv.conf").unwrap();
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!     f.read_to_end(&mut buf).unwrap();
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//!     // Parse the buffer
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!     let cfg = resolv_conf::Config::parse(&buf).unwrap();
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//!     // Print the config
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!     println!("---- Parsed /etc/resolv.conf -----\n{:#?}\n", cfg);
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! }
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! ```
[90](https://docs.rs#90)
[91](https://docs.rs#91)#![warn(missing_debug_implementations, missing_docs, unreachable_pub)]
[92](https://docs.rs#92)#![warn(clippy::use_self)]
[93](https://docs.rs#93)
[94](https://docs.rs#94)use std::fmt;
[95](https://docs.rs#95)use std::iter::Iterator;
[96](https://docs.rs#96)use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr};
[97](https://docs.rs#97)use std::slice::Iter;
[98](https://docs.rs#98)use std::str::{self, from_utf8, FromStr, Utf8Error};
[99](https://docs.rs#99)
[100](https://docs.rs#100)mod ip;
[101](https://docs.rs#101)pub use ip::{AddrParseError, Network, ScopedIp};
[102](https://docs.rs#102)
[103](https://docs.rs#103)/// Represent a resolver configuration, as described in `man 5 resolv.conf`.
[104](https://docs.rs#104)/// The options and defaults match those in the linux `man` page.
[105](https://docs.rs#105)///
[106](https://docs.rs#106)/// Note: while most fields in the structure are public the `search` and
[107](https://docs.rs#107)/// `domain` fields must be accessed via methods. This is because there are
[108](https://docs.rs#108)/// few different ways to treat `domain` field. In GNU libc `search` and
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// `domain` replace each other ([`get_last_search_or_domain`]).
[110](https://docs.rs#110)/// In MacOS `/etc/resolve/*` files `domain` is treated in entirely different
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// way.
[112](https://docs.rs#112)///
[113](https://docs.rs#113)/// Also consider using [`glibc_normalize`] and [`get_system_domain`] to match
[114](https://docs.rs#114)/// behavior of GNU libc.
[115](https://docs.rs#115)///
[116](https://docs.rs#116)/// ```rust
[117](https://docs.rs#117)/// extern crate resolv_conf;
[118](https://docs.rs#118)///
[119](https://docs.rs#119)/// use std::net::Ipv4Addr;
[120](https://docs.rs#120)/// use resolv_conf::{Config, ScopedIp};
[121](https://docs.rs#121)///
[122](https://docs.rs#122)/// fn main() {
[123](https://docs.rs#123)///     // Create a new config
[124](https://docs.rs#124)///     let mut config = Config::new();
[125](https://docs.rs#125)///     config.nameservers.push(ScopedIp::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(8, 8, 8, 8)));
[126](https://docs.rs#126)///     config.set_search(vec!["example.com".into()]);
[127](https://docs.rs#127)///
[128](https://docs.rs#128)///     // Parse a config
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///     let parsed = Config::parse("nameserver 8.8.8.8\nsearch example.com").unwrap();
[130](https://docs.rs#130)///     assert_eq!(parsed, config);
[131](https://docs.rs#131)/// }
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// ```
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///
[134](https://docs.rs#134)/// [`glibc_normalize`]: #method.glibc_normalize
[135](https://docs.rs#135)/// [`get_last_search_or_domain`]: #method.get_last_search_or_domain
[136](https://docs.rs#136)/// [`get_system_domain`]: #method.get_system_domain
[137](https://docs.rs#137)#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[138](https://docs.rs#138)pub struct Config {
[139](https://docs.rs#139)    /// List of nameservers
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    pub nameservers: Vec<ScopedIp>,
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    /// Indicated whether the last line that has been parsed is a "domain" directive or a "search"
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    /// directive. This is important for compatibility with glibc, since in glibc's implementation,
[143](https://docs.rs#143)    /// "search" and "domain" are mutually exclusive, and only the last directive is taken into
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    /// consideration.
[145](https://docs.rs#145)    last_search: LastSearch,
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    /// Domain to append to name when it doesn't contain ndots
[147](https://docs.rs#147)    domain: Option<String>,
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    /// List of suffixes to append to name when it doesn't contain ndots
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    search: Option<Vec<String>>,
[150](https://docs.rs#150)    /// List of preferred addresses
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    pub sortlist: Vec<Network>,
[152](https://docs.rs#152)    /// Enable DNS resolve debugging
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    pub debug: bool,
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    /// Number of dots in name to try absolute resolving first (default 1)
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    pub ndots: u32,
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    /// Dns query timeout (default 5 [sec])
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    pub timeout: u32,
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// Number of attempts to resolve name if server is inaccesible (default 2)
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    pub attempts: u32,
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    /// Round-robin selection of servers (default false)
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    pub rotate: bool,
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    /// Don't check names for validity (default false)
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    pub no_check_names: bool,
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    /// Try AAAA query before A
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    pub inet6: bool,
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    /// Use reverse lookup of ipv6 using bit-label format described instead
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    /// of nibble format
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    pub ip6_bytestring: bool,
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    /// Do ipv6 reverse lookups in ip6.int zone instead of ip6.arpa
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    /// (default false)
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    pub ip6_dotint: bool,
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    /// Enable dns extensions described in RFC 2671
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    pub edns0: bool,
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    /// Don't make ipv4 and ipv6 requests simultaneously
[175](https://docs.rs#175)    pub single_request: bool,
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// Use same socket for the A and AAAA requests
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    pub single_request_reopen: bool,
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    /// Don't resolve unqualified name as top level domain
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    pub no_tld_query: bool,
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    /// Force using TCP for DNS resolution
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    pub use_vc: bool,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    /// Disable the automatic reloading of a changed configuration file
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    pub no_reload: bool,
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    /// Optionally send the AD (authenticated data) bit in queries
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    pub trust_ad: bool,
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    /// The order in which databases should be searched during a lookup
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    /// **(openbsd-only)**
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    pub lookup: Vec<Lookup>,
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    /// The order in which internet protocol families should be prefered
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    /// **(openbsd-only)**
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    pub family: Vec<Family>,
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    /// Suppress AAAA queries made by the stub resolver
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    pub no_aaaa: bool,
[194](https://docs.rs#194)}
[195](https://docs.rs#195)
[196](https://docs.rs#196)impl Config {
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// Create a new `Config` object with default values.
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    ///
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// ```rust
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// # extern crate resolv_conf;
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// use resolv_conf::Config;
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// # fn main() {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    /// let config = Config::new();
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// assert_eq!(config.nameservers, vec![]);
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// assert!(config.get_domain().is_none());
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    /// assert!(config.get_search().is_none());
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    /// assert_eq!(config.sortlist, vec![]);
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    /// assert_eq!(config.debug, false);
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// assert_eq!(config.ndots, 1);
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// assert_eq!(config.timeout, 5);
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// assert_eq!(config.attempts, 2);
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    /// assert_eq!(config.rotate, false);
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// assert_eq!(config.no_check_names, false);
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    /// assert_eq!(config.inet6, false);
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    /// assert_eq!(config.ip6_bytestring, false);
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    /// assert_eq!(config.ip6_dotint, false);
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    /// assert_eq!(config.edns0, false);
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    /// assert_eq!(config.single_request, false);
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    /// assert_eq!(config.single_request_reopen, false);
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// assert_eq!(config.no_tld_query, false);
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    /// assert_eq!(config.use_vc, false);
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// # }
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[224](https://docs.rs#224)        Self::default()
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// Parse a buffer and return the corresponding `Config` object.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    ///
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    /// ```rust
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    /// # extern crate resolv_conf;
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    /// use resolv_conf::{ScopedIp, Config};
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    /// # fn main() {
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    /// let config_str = "# /etc/resolv.conf
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    /// nameserver  8.8.8.8
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    /// nameserver  8.8.4.4
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    /// search      example.com sub.example.com
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    /// options     ndots:8 attempts:8";
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    ///
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// // Parse the config
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    /// let parsed_config = Config::parse(&config_str).expect("Failed to parse config");
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    ///
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    /// // Print the config
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    /// println!("{:?}", parsed_config);
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    /// # }
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    /// ```
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    pub fn parse<T: AsRef<[u8]>>(buf: T) -> Result<Self, ParseError> {
[247](https://docs.rs#247)        let (new, mut errors) = Self::parse_with_errors(buf.as_ref());
[248](https://docs.rs#248)        let mut iter = errors.drain(..);
[249](https://docs.rs#249)        match iter.next() {
[250](https://docs.rs#250)            Some(err) => Err(err),
[251](https://docs.rs#251)            None => Ok(new),
[252](https://docs.rs#252)        }
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    }
[254](https://docs.rs#254)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    /// Parse a buffer and return a best-effort parsed `Config` object along with any errors.
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    pub fn parse_with_errors(bytes: &[u8]) -> (Self, Vec<ParseError>) {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)        use ParseError::*;
[258](https://docs.rs#258)        let mut cfg = Self::new();
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        let mut errors = Vec::new();
[260](https://docs.rs#260)        'lines: for (lineno, line) in bytes.split(|&x| x == b'\n').enumerate() {
[261](https://docs.rs#261)            for &c in line.iter() {
[262](https://docs.rs#262)                if c != b'\t' && c != b' ' {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)                    if c == b';' || c == b'#' {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                        continue 'lines;
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                    } else {
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                        break;
[267](https://docs.rs#267)                    }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)                }
[269](https://docs.rs#269)            }
[270](https://docs.rs#270)
[271](https://docs.rs#271)            // All that dances above to allow invalid utf-8 inside the comments
[272](https://docs.rs#272)            let str = match from_utf8(line) {
[273](https://docs.rs#273)                Ok(str) => str,
[274](https://docs.rs#274)                Err(e) => {
[275](https://docs.rs#275)                    errors.push(InvalidUtf8(lineno, e));
[276](https://docs.rs#276)                    continue;
[277](https://docs.rs#277)                }
[278](https://docs.rs#278)            };
[279](https://docs.rs#279)
[280](https://docs.rs#280)            // ignore everything after ';' or '#'
[281](https://docs.rs#281)            let text = match str.split([';', '#']).next() {
[282](https://docs.rs#282)                Some(text) => text,
[283](https://docs.rs#283)                None => {
[284](https://docs.rs#284)                    errors.push(InvalidValue(lineno));
[285](https://docs.rs#285)                    continue;
[286](https://docs.rs#286)                }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)            };
[288](https://docs.rs#288)
[289](https://docs.rs#289)            let mut words = text.split_whitespace();
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            let keyword = match words.next() {
[291](https://docs.rs#291)                Some(x) => x,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)                None => continue,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            };
[294](https://docs.rs#294)
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            match keyword {
[296](https://docs.rs#296)                "nameserver" => {
[297](https://docs.rs#297)                    let srv = match words.next() {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)                        Some(srv) => srv,
[299](https://docs.rs#299)                        None => {
[300](https://docs.rs#300)                            errors.push(InvalidValue(lineno));
[301](https://docs.rs#301)                            continue;
[302](https://docs.rs#302)                        }
[303](https://docs.rs#303)                    };
[304](https://docs.rs#304)
[305](https://docs.rs#305)                    match ScopedIp::from_str(srv) {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)                        Ok(addr) => cfg.nameservers.push(addr),
[307](https://docs.rs#307)                        Err(e) => errors.push(InvalidIp(lineno, e)),
[308](https://docs.rs#308)                    }
[309](https://docs.rs#309)
[310](https://docs.rs#310)                    if words.next().is_some() {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)                        errors.push(ExtraData(lineno));
[312](https://docs.rs#312)                    }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                }
[314](https://docs.rs#314)                "domain" => {
[315](https://docs.rs#315)                    let domain = match words.next() {
[316](https://docs.rs#316)                        Some(domain) => domain,
[317](https://docs.rs#317)                        None => {
[318](https://docs.rs#318)                            errors.push(InvalidValue(lineno));
[319](https://docs.rs#319)                            continue;
[320](https://docs.rs#320)                        }
[321](https://docs.rs#321)                    };
[322](https://docs.rs#322)
[323](https://docs.rs#323)                    cfg.set_domain(domain.to_owned());
[324](https://docs.rs#324)                    if words.next().is_some() {
[325](https://docs.rs#325)                        errors.push(ExtraData(lineno));
[326](https://docs.rs#326)                    }
[327](https://docs.rs#327)                }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)                "search" => {
[329](https://docs.rs#329)                    let mut search = Vec::new();
[330](https://docs.rs#330)                    for word in words {
[331](https://docs.rs#331)                        if !word.contains(',') {
[332](https://docs.rs#332)                            // Easy to get confused between spaces and commas here
[333](https://docs.rs#333)                            // https://github.com/hickory-dns/resolv-conf/issues/58
[334](https://docs.rs#334)                            search.push(word.to_owned());
[335](https://docs.rs#335)                        }
[336](https://docs.rs#336)                    }
[337](https://docs.rs#337)                    cfg.set_search(search);
[338](https://docs.rs#338)                }
[339](https://docs.rs#339)                "sortlist" => {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)                    cfg.sortlist.clear();
[341](https://docs.rs#341)                    for pair in words {
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                        match Network::from_str(pair) {
[343](https://docs.rs#343)                            Ok(network) => cfg.sortlist.push(network),
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                            Err(e) => errors.push(InvalidIp(lineno, e)),
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                        }
[346](https://docs.rs#346)                    }
[347](https://docs.rs#347)                }
[348](https://docs.rs#348)                "options" => {
[349](https://docs.rs#349)                    for pair in words {
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                        let mut iter = pair.splitn(2, ':');
[351](https://docs.rs#351)                        let key = match iter.next() {
[352](https://docs.rs#352)                            Some(key) => key,
[353](https://docs.rs#353)                            None => {
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                                errors.push(InvalidValue(lineno));
[355](https://docs.rs#355)                                continue 'lines;
[356](https://docs.rs#356)                            }
[357](https://docs.rs#357)                        };
[358](https://docs.rs#358)
[359](https://docs.rs#359)                        let value = iter.next();
[360](https://docs.rs#360)                        if iter.next().is_some() {
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                            errors.push(ExtraData(lineno));
[362](https://docs.rs#362)                            continue 'lines;
[363](https://docs.rs#363)                        }
[364](https://docs.rs#364)
[365](https://docs.rs#365)                        match (key, value) {
[366](https://docs.rs#366)                            // TODO(tailhook) ensure that values are None?
[367](https://docs.rs#367)                            ("debug", _) => cfg.debug = true,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)                            ("ndots", Some(x)) => match u32::from_str(x) {
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                                Ok(ndots) => cfg.ndots = ndots,
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                                Err(_) => errors.push(InvalidOptionValue(lineno)),
[371](https://docs.rs#371)                            },
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                            ("timeout", Some(x)) => match u32::from_str(x) {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                                Ok(timeout) => cfg.timeout = timeout,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)                                Err(_) => errors.push(InvalidOptionValue(lineno)),
[375](https://docs.rs#375)                            },
[376](https://docs.rs#376)                            ("attempts", Some(x)) => match u32::from_str(x) {
[377](https://docs.rs#377)                                Ok(attempts) => cfg.attempts = attempts,
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                                Err(_) => errors.push(InvalidOptionValue(lineno)),
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                            },
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                            ("rotate", _) => cfg.rotate = true,
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                            ("no-check-names", _) => cfg.no_check_names = true,
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                            ("inet6", _) => cfg.inet6 = true,
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                            ("ip6-bytestring", _) => cfg.ip6_bytestring = true,
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                            ("ip6-dotint", _) => cfg.ip6_dotint = true,
[385](https://docs.rs#385)                            ("no-ip6-dotint", _) => cfg.ip6_dotint = false,
[386](https://docs.rs#386)                            ("edns0", _) => cfg.edns0 = true,
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                            ("single-request", _) => cfg.single_request = true,
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                            ("single-request-reopen", _) => cfg.single_request_reopen = true,
[389](https://docs.rs#389)                            ("no-reload", _) => cfg.no_reload = true,
[390](https://docs.rs#390)                            ("trust-ad", _) => cfg.trust_ad = true,
[391](https://docs.rs#391)                            ("no-tld-query", _) => cfg.no_tld_query = true,
[392](https://docs.rs#392)                            ("use-vc", _) => cfg.use_vc = true,
[393](https://docs.rs#393)                            ("no-aaaa", _) => cfg.no_aaaa = true,
[394](https://docs.rs#394)                            _ => errors.push(InvalidOption(lineno)),
[395](https://docs.rs#395)                        }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)                    }
[397](https://docs.rs#397)                }
[398](https://docs.rs#398)                "lookup" => {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)                    for word in words {
[400](https://docs.rs#400)                        match word {
[401](https://docs.rs#401)                            "file" => cfg.lookup.push(Lookup::File),
[402](https://docs.rs#402)                            "bind" => cfg.lookup.push(Lookup::Bind),
[403](https://docs.rs#403)                            extra => cfg.lookup.push(Lookup::Extra(extra.to_string())),
[404](https://docs.rs#404)                        }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)                    }
[406](https://docs.rs#406)                }
[407](https://docs.rs#407)                "family" => {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)                    for word in words {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                        match word {
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                            "inet4" => cfg.family.push(Family::Inet4),
[411](https://docs.rs#411)                            "inet6" => cfg.family.push(Family::Inet6),
[412](https://docs.rs#412)                            _ => errors.push(InvalidValue(lineno)),
[413](https://docs.rs#413)                        }
[414](https://docs.rs#414)                    }
[415](https://docs.rs#415)                }
[416](https://docs.rs#416)                _ => errors.push(InvalidDirective(lineno)),
[417](https://docs.rs#417)            }
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        }
[419](https://docs.rs#419)
[420](https://docs.rs#420)        (cfg, errors)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    }
[422](https://docs.rs#422)
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    /// Return the suffixes declared in the last "domain" or "search" directive.
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    ///
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    /// ```rust
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    /// # extern crate resolv_conf;
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// use resolv_conf::{ScopedIp, Config};
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    /// # fn main() {
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    /// let config_str = "search example.com sub.example.com\ndomain localdomain";
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    /// let parsed_config = Config::parse(&config_str).expect("Failed to parse config");
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    /// let domains = parsed_config.get_last_search_or_domain()
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    ///                            .map(|domain| domain.clone())
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    ///                            .collect::<Vec<String>>();
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    /// assert_eq!(domains, vec![String::from("localdomain")]);
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    ///
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    /// let config_str = "domain localdomain\nsearch example.com sub.example.com";
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    /// let parsed_config = Config::parse(&config_str).expect("Failed to parse config");
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    /// let domains = parsed_config.get_last_search_or_domain()
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    ///                            .map(|domain| domain.clone())
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    ///                            .collect::<Vec<String>>();
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    /// assert_eq!(domains, vec![String::from("example.com"), String::from("sub.example.com")]);
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    /// # }
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    pub fn get_last_search_or_domain(&self) -> DomainIter<'_> {
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        let domain_iter = match self.last_search {
[445](https://docs.rs#445)            LastSearch::Search => {
[446](https://docs.rs#446)                DomainIterInternal::Search(self.get_search().map(|domains| domains.iter()))
[447](https://docs.rs#447)            }
[448](https://docs.rs#448)            LastSearch::Domain => DomainIterInternal::Domain(self.get_domain()),
[449](https://docs.rs#449)            LastSearch::None => DomainIterInternal::None,
[450](https://docs.rs#450)        };
[451](https://docs.rs#451)        DomainIter(domain_iter)
[452](https://docs.rs#452)    }

[476](https://docs.rs#476)    /// Normalize config according to glibc rulees
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    ///
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    /// Currently this method does the following things:
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    ///
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    /// 1. Truncates list of nameservers to 3 at max
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    /// 2. Truncates search list to 6 at max
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    ///
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    /// Other normalizations may be added in future as long as they hold true
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    /// for a particular GNU libc implementation.
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    ///
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    /// Note: this method is not called after parsing, because we think it's
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    /// not forward-compatible to rely on such small and ugly limits. Still,
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    /// it's useful to keep implementation as close to glibc as possible.
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    pub fn glibc_normalize(&mut self) {
[490](https://docs.rs#490)        self.nameservers.truncate(NAMESERVER_LIMIT);
[491](https://docs.rs#491)        self.search = self.search.take().map(|mut s| {
[492](https://docs.rs#492)            s.truncate(SEARCH_LIMIT);
[493](https://docs.rs#493)            s
[494](https://docs.rs#494)        });
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    }
[496](https://docs.rs#496)
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    /// Get nameserver or on the local machine
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    pub fn get_nameservers_or_local(&self) -> Vec<ScopedIp> {
[499](https://docs.rs#499)        if self.nameservers.is_empty() {
[500](https://docs.rs#500)            vec![
[501](https://docs.rs#501)                ScopedIp::from(IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(127, 0, 0, 1))),
[502](https://docs.rs#502)                ScopedIp::from(IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::new(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))),
[503](https://docs.rs#503)            ]
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        } else {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)            self.nameservers.to_vec()
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        }
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    }
[508](https://docs.rs#508)
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    /// Get domain from config or fallback to the suffix of a hostname
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    ///
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    /// This is how glibc finds out a hostname.
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    pub fn get_system_domain(&self) -> Option<String> {
[513](https://docs.rs#513)        if self.domain.is_some() {
[514](https://docs.rs#514)            return self.domain.clone();
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        }
[516](https://docs.rs#516)
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        // This buffer is far larger than what most systems will ever allow, eg.
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        // linux uses 64 via _SC_HOST_NAME_MAX even though POSIX says the size
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        // must be _at least_ _POSIX_HOST_NAME_MAX (255), but other systems can
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        // be larger, so we just use a sufficiently sized buffer so we can defer
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        // a heap allocation until the last possible moment.
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        let mut hostname = [0u8; 1024];
[523](https://docs.rs#523)
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_feature = "crt-static"))]
[525](https://docs.rs#525)        {
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            use std::{fs::File, io::Read};
[527](https://docs.rs#527)            let mut file = File::open("/proc/sys/kernel/hostname").ok()?;
[528](https://docs.rs#528)            let read_bytes = file.read(&mut hostname).ok()?;
[529](https://docs.rs#529)
[530](https://docs.rs#530)            // According to Linux kernel's proc_dostring handler, user-space reads
[531](https://docs.rs#531)            // of /proc/sys entries which have a string value are terminated by
[532](https://docs.rs#532)            // a newline character. While libc gethostname() terminates the hostname
[533](https://docs.rs#533)            // with a null character. Hence, to match the behavior of gethostname()
[534](https://docs.rs#534)            // it is necessary to replace the newline with a null character.
[535](https://docs.rs#535)            if read_bytes == hostname.len() && hostname[read_bytes - 1] != b'\n' {
[536](https://docs.rs#536)                // In this case the string read from /proc/sys/kernel/hostname is
[537](https://docs.rs#537)                // truncated and cannot be terminated by a null character
[538](https://docs.rs#538)                return None;
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            }
[540](https://docs.rs#540)            // Since any non-truncated string read from /proc/sys/kernel/hostname
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            // ends with a newline character, read_bytes > 0.
[542](https://docs.rs#542)            hostname[read_bytes - 1] = 0;
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        }
[544](https://docs.rs#544)
[545](https://docs.rs#545)        #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "linux", target_feature = "crt-static")))]
[546](https://docs.rs#546)        {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            /*unsafe*/
[548](https://docs.rs#548)            extern "C" {
[549](https://docs.rs#549)                fn gethostname(hostname: *mut u8, size: usize) -> i32;
[550](https://docs.rs#550)            }
[551](https://docs.rs#551)
[552](https://docs.rs#552)            unsafe {
[553](https://docs.rs#553)                if gethostname(hostname.as_mut_ptr(), hostname.len()) < 0 {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)                    return None;
[555](https://docs.rs#555)                }
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            }
[557](https://docs.rs#557)        }
[558](https://docs.rs#558)
[559](https://docs.rs#559)        domain_from_host(&hostname).map(|s| s.to_owned())
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)}

[594](https://docs.rs#594)impl fmt::Display for Config {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    fn fmt(&self, fmt: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        let Self {
[597](https://docs.rs#597)            nameservers,
[598](https://docs.rs#598)            last_search,
[599](https://docs.rs#599)            domain,
[600](https://docs.rs#600)            search,
[601](https://docs.rs#601)            sortlist,
[602](https://docs.rs#602)            debug,
[603](https://docs.rs#603)            ndots,
[604](https://docs.rs#604)            timeout,
[605](https://docs.rs#605)            attempts,
[606](https://docs.rs#606)            rotate,
[607](https://docs.rs#607)            no_check_names,
[608](https://docs.rs#608)            inet6,
[609](https://docs.rs#609)            ip6_bytestring,
[610](https://docs.rs#610)            ip6_dotint,
[611](https://docs.rs#611)            edns0,
[612](https://docs.rs#612)            single_request,
[613](https://docs.rs#613)            single_request_reopen,
[614](https://docs.rs#614)            no_tld_query,
[615](https://docs.rs#615)            use_vc,
[616](https://docs.rs#616)            no_reload,
[617](https://docs.rs#617)            trust_ad,
[618](https://docs.rs#618)            lookup,
[619](https://docs.rs#619)            family,
[620](https://docs.rs#620)            no_aaaa,
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        } = self;
[622](https://docs.rs#622)
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        for nameserver in nameservers.iter() {
[624](https://docs.rs#624)            writeln!(fmt, "nameserver {nameserver}")?;
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        }
[626](https://docs.rs#626)
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        if last_search != &LastSearch::Domain {
[628](https://docs.rs#628)            if let Some(domain) = domain {
[629](https://docs.rs#629)                writeln!(fmt, "domain {domain}")?;
[630](https://docs.rs#630)            }
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        }
[632](https://docs.rs#632)
[633](https://docs.rs#633)        if let Some(search) = search {
[634](https://docs.rs#634)            if !search.is_empty() {
[635](https://docs.rs#635)                write!(fmt, "search")?;
[636](https://docs.rs#636)                for suffix in search.iter() {
[637](https://docs.rs#637)                    write!(fmt, " {suffix}")?;
[638](https://docs.rs#638)                }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)                writeln!(fmt)?;
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            }
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)
[643](https://docs.rs#643)        if last_search == &LastSearch::Domain {
[644](https://docs.rs#644)            if let Some(domain) = &self.domain {
[645](https://docs.rs#645)                writeln!(fmt, "domain {domain}")?;
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            }
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        }
[648](https://docs.rs#648)
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        if !sortlist.is_empty() {
[650](https://docs.rs#650)            write!(fmt, "sortlist")?;
[651](https://docs.rs#651)            for network in sortlist.iter() {
[652](https://docs.rs#652)                write!(fmt, " {network}")?;
[653](https://docs.rs#653)            }
[654](https://docs.rs#654)            writeln!(fmt)?;
[655](https://docs.rs#655)        }
[656](https://docs.rs#656)
[657](https://docs.rs#657)        if !lookup.is_empty() {
[658](https://docs.rs#658)            write!(fmt, "lookup")?;
[659](https://docs.rs#659)            for db in lookup.iter() {
[660](https://docs.rs#660)                match db {
[661](https://docs.rs#661)                    Lookup::File => write!(fmt, " file")?,
[662](https://docs.rs#662)                    Lookup::Bind => write!(fmt, " bind")?,
[663](https://docs.rs#663)                    Lookup::Extra(extra) => write!(fmt, " {extra}")?,
[664](https://docs.rs#664)                }
[665](https://docs.rs#665)            }
[666](https://docs.rs#666)            writeln!(fmt)?;
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        }
[668](https://docs.rs#668)
[669](https://docs.rs#669)        if !family.is_empty() {
[670](https://docs.rs#670)            write!(fmt, "family")?;
[671](https://docs.rs#671)            for fam in family.iter() {
[672](https://docs.rs#672)                match fam {
[673](https://docs.rs#673)                    Family::Inet4 => write!(fmt, " inet4")?,
[674](https://docs.rs#674)                    Family::Inet6 => write!(fmt, " inet6")?,
[675](https://docs.rs#675)                }
[676](https://docs.rs#676)            }
[677](https://docs.rs#677)            writeln!(fmt)?;
[678](https://docs.rs#678)        }
[679](https://docs.rs#679)
[680](https://docs.rs#680)        if *debug {
[681](https://docs.rs#681)            writeln!(fmt, "options debug")?;
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        }
[683](https://docs.rs#683)        if *ndots != 1 {
[684](https://docs.rs#684)            writeln!(fmt, "options ndots:{}", self.ndots)?;
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        }
[686](https://docs.rs#686)        if *timeout != 5 {
[687](https://docs.rs#687)            writeln!(fmt, "options timeout:{}", self.timeout)?;
[688](https://docs.rs#688)        }
[689](https://docs.rs#689)        if *attempts != 2 {
[690](https://docs.rs#690)            writeln!(fmt, "options attempts:{}", self.attempts)?;
[691](https://docs.rs#691)        }
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        if *rotate {
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            writeln!(fmt, "options rotate")?;
[694](https://docs.rs#694)        }
[695](https://docs.rs#695)        if *no_check_names {
[696](https://docs.rs#696)            writeln!(fmt, "options no-check-names")?;
[697](https://docs.rs#697)        }
[698](https://docs.rs#698)        if *inet6 {
[699](https://docs.rs#699)            writeln!(fmt, "options inet6")?;
[700](https://docs.rs#700)        }
[701](https://docs.rs#701)        if *ip6_bytestring {
[702](https://docs.rs#702)            writeln!(fmt, "options ip6-bytestring")?;
[703](https://docs.rs#703)        }
[704](https://docs.rs#704)        if *ip6_dotint {
[705](https://docs.rs#705)            writeln!(fmt, "options ip6-dotint")?;
[706](https://docs.rs#706)        }
[707](https://docs.rs#707)        if *edns0 {
[708](https://docs.rs#708)            writeln!(fmt, "options edns0")?;
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        }
[710](https://docs.rs#710)        if *single_request {
[711](https://docs.rs#711)            writeln!(fmt, "options single-request")?;
[712](https://docs.rs#712)        }
[713](https://docs.rs#713)        if *single_request_reopen {
[714](https://docs.rs#714)            writeln!(fmt, "options single-request-reopen")?;
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        }
[716](https://docs.rs#716)        if *no_tld_query {
[717](https://docs.rs#717)            writeln!(fmt, "options no-tld-query")?;
[718](https://docs.rs#718)        }
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        if *use_vc {
[720](https://docs.rs#720)            writeln!(fmt, "options use-vc")?;
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        }
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        if *no_reload {
[723](https://docs.rs#723)            writeln!(fmt, "options no-reload")?;
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        }
[725](https://docs.rs#725)        if *trust_ad {
[726](https://docs.rs#726)            writeln!(fmt, "options trust-ad")?;
[727](https://docs.rs#727)        }
[728](https://docs.rs#728)        if *no_aaaa {
[729](https://docs.rs#729)            writeln!(fmt, "options no-aaaa")?;
[730](https://docs.rs#730)        }
[731](https://docs.rs#731)
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        Ok(())
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    }

[736](https://docs.rs#736)/// Error while parsing resolv.conf file
[737](https://docs.rs#737)#[derive(Debug)]
[738](https://docs.rs#738)pub enum ParseError {
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    /// Error that may be returned when the string to parse contains invalid UTF-8 sequences
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    InvalidUtf8(usize, Utf8Error),
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    /// Error returned a value for a given directive is invalid.
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    /// This can also happen when the value is missing, if the directive requires a value.
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    InvalidValue(usize),
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    /// Error returned when a value for a given option is invalid.
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    /// This can also happen when the value is missing, if the option requires a value.
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    InvalidOptionValue(usize),
[747](https://docs.rs#747)    /// Error returned when a invalid option is found.
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    InvalidOption(usize),
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    /// Error returned when a invalid directive is found.
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    InvalidDirective(usize),
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    /// Error returned when a value cannot be parsed an an IP address.
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    InvalidIp(usize, AddrParseError),
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    /// Error returned when there is extra data at the end of a line.
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    ExtraData(usize),
[755](https://docs.rs#755)}
[756](https://docs.rs#756)
[757](https://docs.rs#757)impl std::fmt::Display for ParseError {
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter) -> std::fmt::Result {
[759](https://docs.rs#759)        match self {
[760](https://docs.rs#760)            Self::InvalidUtf8(line, err) => write!(f, "bad unicode at line {line}: {err}"),
[761](https://docs.rs#761)            Self::InvalidValue(line) => write!(
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                f,
[763](https://docs.rs#763)                "directive at line {line} is improperly formatted or contains invalid value",
[764](https://docs.rs#764)            ),
[765](https://docs.rs#765)            Self::InvalidOptionValue(line) => write!(
[766](https://docs.rs#766)                f,
[767](https://docs.rs#767)                "directive options at line {line} contains invalid value of some option",
[768](https://docs.rs#768)            ),
[769](https://docs.rs#769)            Self::InvalidOption(line) => {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)                write!(f, "option at line {line} is not recognized")
[771](https://docs.rs#771)            }
[772](https://docs.rs#772)            Self::InvalidDirective(line) => {
[773](https://docs.rs#773)                write!(f, "directive at line {line} is not recognized")
[774](https://docs.rs#774)            }
[775](https://docs.rs#775)            Self::InvalidIp(line, err) => {
[776](https://docs.rs#776)                write!(f, "directive at line {line} contains invalid IP: {err}")
[777](https://docs.rs#777)            }
[778](https://docs.rs#778)            Self::ExtraData(line) => write!(f, "extra data at the end of line {line}"),
[779](https://docs.rs#779)        }
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    }
[781](https://docs.rs#781)}
[782](https://docs.rs#782)
[783](https://docs.rs#783)impl std::error::Error for ParseError {
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
[785](https://docs.rs#785)        match self {
[786](https://docs.rs#786)            Self::InvalidUtf8(_, err) => Some(err),
[787](https://docs.rs#787)            _ => None,
[788](https://docs.rs#788)        }
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    }

[791](https://docs.rs#791)
[792](https://docs.rs#792)/// An iterator returned by [`Config.get_last_search_or_domain`](struct.Config.html#method.get_last_search_or_domain)
[793](https://docs.rs#793)#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
[794](https://docs.rs#794)pub struct DomainIter<'a>(DomainIterInternal<'a>);
[795](https://docs.rs#795)
[796](https://docs.rs#796)impl<'a> Iterator for DomainIter<'a> {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    type Item = &'a String;
[798](https://docs.rs#798)
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
[800](https://docs.rs#800)        self.0.next()

[845](https://docs.rs#845)/// Parses the domain name from a hostname, if available
[846](https://docs.rs#846)fn domain_from_host(hostname: &[u8]) -> Option<&str> {
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    let mut start = None;
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    for (i, b) in hostname.iter().copied().enumerate() {
[849](https://docs.rs#849)        if b == b'.' && start.is_none() {
[850](https://docs.rs#850)            start = Some(i);
[851](https://docs.rs#851)            continue;
[852](https://docs.rs#852)        } else if b > 0 {
[853](https://docs.rs#853)            continue;
[854](https://docs.rs#854)        }
[855](https://docs.rs#855)
[856](https://docs.rs#856)        return match start? {
[857](https://docs.rs#857)            // Avoid empty domains
[858](https://docs.rs#858)            start if i - start < 2 => None,
[859](https://docs.rs#859)            start => str::from_utf8(&hostname[start + 1..i]).ok(),
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        };
[861](https://docs.rs#861)    }
[862](https://docs.rs#862)
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    None
[864](https://docs.rs#864)}
[865](https://docs.rs#865)

    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

Represent a resolver configuration, as described in `man 5 resolv.conf`.
The options and defaults match those in the linux `man` page.

Note: while most fields in the structure are public the `search` and
`domain` fields must be accessed via methods. This is because there are
few different ways to treat `domain` field. In GNU libc `search` and
`domain` replace each other ([ get_last_search_or_domain](https://docs.rs#method.get_last_search_or_domain)).
In MacOS

`/etc/resolve/*` files `domain` is treated in entirely different
way.Also consider using [ glibc_normalize](https://docs.rs#method.glibc_normalize) and

[to match behavior of GNU libc.](https://docs.rs#method.get_system_domain)

`get_system_domain````
extern crate resolv_conf;
use std::net::Ipv4Addr;
use resolv_conf::{Config, ScopedIp};
fn main() {
    // Create a new config
    let mut config = Config::new();
    config.nameservers.push(ScopedIp::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(8, 8, 8, 8)));
    config.set_search(vec!["example.com".into()]);
    // Parse a config
    let parsed = Config::parse("nameserver 8.8.8.8\nsearch example.com").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(parsed, config);
}
```

use resolv_conf::{ScopedIp, Config};
let config_str = "# /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver  8.8.8.8
nameserver  8.8.4.4
search      example.com sub.example.com
options     ndots:8 attempts:8";
// Parse the config
let parsed_config = Config::parse(&config_str).expect("Failed to parse config");
// Print the config
println!("{:?}", parsed_config);

#### pub fn [get_last_search_or_domain](https://docs.rs#method.get_last_search_or_domain)(&self) -> [DomainIter](https://docs.rs/struct.DomainIter.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Return the suffixes declared in the last “domain” or “search” directive.

```
use resolv_conf::{ScopedIp, Config};
let config_str = "search example.com sub.example.com\ndomain localdomain";
let parsed_config = Config::parse(&config_str).expect("Failed to parse config");
let domains = parsed_config.get_last_search_or_domain()
                           .map(|domain| domain.clone())
                           .collect::<Vec<String>>();
assert_eq!(domains, vec![String::from("localdomain")]);
let config_str = "domain localdomain\nsearch example.com sub.example.com";
let parsed_config = Config::parse(&config_str).expect("Failed to parse config");
let domains = parsed_config.get_last_search_or_domain()
                           .map(|domain| domain.clone())
                           .collect::<Vec<String>>();
assert_eq!(domains, vec![String::from("example.com"), String::from("sub.example.com")]);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/resolv_conf/lib.rs.html#489-495)#### pub fn [glibc_normalize](https://docs.rs#method.glibc_normalize)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/resolv_conf/lib.rs.html#489-495)

#### pub fn [glibc_normalize](https://docs.rs#method.glibc_normalize)(&mut self)

Normalize config according to glibc rulees

Currently this method does the following things:

- Truncates list of nameservers to 3 at max
- Truncates search list to 6 at max

Other normalizations may be added in future as long as they hold true for a particular GNU libc implementation.

Note: this method is not called after parsing, because we think it’s not forward-compatible to rely on such small and ugly limits. Still, it’s useful to keep implementation as close to glibc as possible.

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2

## Expand description

`clap` is a simple-to-use, efficient, and full-featured library for parsing command line
arguments and subcommands when writing console/terminal applications.

`clap` is used to parse *and validate* the string of command line arguments provided by the user
at runtime. You provide the list of valid possibilities, and `clap` handles the rest. This means
you focus on your *applications* functionality, and less on the parsing and validating of
arguments.

`clap` also provides the traditional version and help switches (or flags) ‘for free’ meaning
automatically with no configuration. It does this by checking the list of valid possibilities you
supplied and adding only the ones you haven’t already defined. If you are using subcommands,
`clap` will also auto-generate a `help` subcommand for you in addition to the traditional flags.

Once `clap` parses the user provided string of arguments, it returns the matches along with any
applicable values. If the user made an error or typo, `clap` informs them of the mistake and
exits gracefully (or returns a `Result` type and allows you to perform any clean up prior to
exit). Because of this, you can make reasonable assumptions in your code about the validity of
the arguments.

The following examples show a quick example of some of the very basic functionality of `clap`.
For more advanced usage, such as requirements, conflicts, groups, multiple values and
occurrences see the [documentation](https://docs.rs/clap/), [examples/](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/v2.34.0/examples) directory of
this repository or the [video tutorials](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLza5oFLQGTl2Z5T8g1pRkIynR3E0_pc7U).

**NOTE:** All of these examples are functionally the same, but show different styles in which to
use `clap`

The first example shows a method that allows more advanced configuration options (not shown in this small example), or even dynamically generating arguments when desired. The downside is it’s more verbose.

```
// (Full example with detailed comments in examples/01b_quick_example.rs)
//
// This example demonstrates clap's full 'builder pattern' style of creating arguments which is
// more verbose, but allows easier editing, and at times more advanced options, or the possibility
// to generate arguments dynamically.
extern crate clap;
use clap::{Arg, App, SubCommand};
fn main() {
    let matches = App::new("My Super Program")
                          .version("1.0")
                          .author("Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>")
                          .about("Does awesome things")
                          .arg(Arg::with_name("config")
                               .short("c")
                               .long("config")
                               .value_name("FILE")
                               .help("Sets a custom config file")
                               .takes_value(true))
                          .arg(Arg::with_name("INPUT")
                               .help("Sets the input file to use")
                               .required(true)
                               .index(1))
                          .arg(Arg::with_name("v")
                               .short("v")
                               .multiple(true)
                               .help("Sets the level of verbosity"))
                          .subcommand(SubCommand::with_name("test")
                                      .about("controls testing features")
                                      .version("1.3")
                                      .author("Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>")
                                      .arg(Arg::with_name("debug")
                                          .short("d")
                                          .help("print debug information verbosely")))
                          .get_matches();
    // Gets a value for config if supplied by user, or defaults to "default.conf"
    let config = matches.value_of("config").unwrap_or("default.conf");
    println!("Value for config: {}", config);
    // Calling .unwrap() is safe here because "INPUT" is required (if "INPUT" wasn't
    // required we could have used an 'if let' to conditionally get the value)
    println!("Using input file: {}", matches.value_of("INPUT").unwrap());
    // Vary the output based on how many times the user used the "verbose" flag
    // (i.e. 'myprog -v -v -v' or 'myprog -vvv' vs 'myprog -v'
    match matches.occurrences_of("v") {
        0 => println!("No verbose info"),
        1 => println!("Some verbose info"),
        2 => println!("Tons of verbose info"),
        3 | _ => println!("Don't be crazy"),
    }
    // You can handle information about subcommands by requesting their matches by name
    // (as below), requesting just the name used, or both at the same time
    if let Some(matches) = matches.subcommand_matches("test") {
        if matches.is_present("debug") {
            println!("Printing debug info...");
        } else {
            println!("Printing normally...");
        }
    }
    // more program logic goes here...
}
```
The next example shows a far less verbose method, but sacrifices some of the advanced
configuration options (not shown in this small example). This method also takes a *very* minor
runtime penalty.

```
// (Full example with detailed comments in examples/01a_quick_example.rs)
//
// This example demonstrates clap's "usage strings" method of creating arguments
// which is less verbose
extern crate clap;
use clap::{Arg, App, SubCommand};
fn main() {
    let matches = App::new("myapp")
                          .version("1.0")
                          .author("Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>")
                          .about("Does awesome things")
                          .args_from_usage(
                              "-c, --config=[FILE] 'Sets a custom config file'
                              <INPUT>              'Sets the input file to use'
                              -v...                'Sets the level of verbosity'")
                          .subcommand(SubCommand::with_name("test")
                                      .about("controls testing features")
                                      .version("1.3")
                                      .author("Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>")
                                      .arg_from_usage("-d, --debug 'Print debug information'"))
                          .get_matches();
    // Same as previous example...
}
```
This third method shows how you can use a YAML file to build your CLI and keep your Rust source tidy or support multiple localized translations by having different YAML files for each localization.

First, create the `cli.yml` file to hold your CLI options, but it could be called anything we
like:

```
name: myapp
version: "1.0"
author: Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>
about: Does awesome things
args:
    - config:
        short: c
        long: config
        value_name: FILE
        help: Sets a custom config file
        takes_value: true
    - INPUT:
        help: Sets the input file to use
        required: true
        index: 1
    - verbose:
        short: v
        multiple: true
        help: Sets the level of verbosity
subcommands:
    - test:
        about: controls testing features
        version: "1.3"
        author: Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>
        args:
            - debug:
                short: d
                help: print debug information
```
Since this feature requires additional dependencies that not everyone may want, it is *not*
compiled in by default and we need to enable a feature flag in Cargo.toml:

Simply change your `clap = "~2.27.0"` to `clap = {version = "~2.27.0", features = ["yaml"]}`.

At last we create our `main.rs` file just like we would have with the previous two examples:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// (Full example with detailed comments in examples/17_yaml.rs)
//
// This example demonstrates clap's building from YAML style of creating arguments which is far
// more clean, but takes a very small performance hit compared to the other two methods.
#[macro_use]
extern crate clap;
use clap::App;
fn main() {
    // The YAML file is found relative to the current file, similar to how modules are found
    let yaml = load_yaml!("cli.yml");
    let matches = App::from_yaml(yaml).get_matches();
    // Same as previous examples...
}
```
Finally there is a macro version, which is like a hybrid approach offering the speed of the builder pattern (the first example), but without all the verbosity.

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate clap;
fn main() {
    let matches = clap_app!(myapp =>
        (version: "1.0")
        (author: "Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>")
        (about: "Does awesome things")
        (@arg CONFIG: -c --config +takes_value "Sets a custom config file")
        (@arg INPUT: +required "Sets the input file to use")
        (@arg debug: -d ... "Sets the level of debugging information")
        (@subcommand test =>
            (about: "controls testing features")
            (version: "1.3")
            (author: "Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>")
            (@arg verbose: -v --verbose "Print test information verbosely")
        )
    ).get_matches();
    // Same as before...
}
```
If you were to compile any of the above programs and run them with the flag `--help` or `-h` (or
`help` subcommand, since we defined `test` as a subcommand) the following would be output

```
$ myprog --help
My Super Program 1.0
Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>
Does awesome things
USAGE:
    MyApp [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <INPUT> [SUBCOMMAND]
FLAGS:
    -h, --help       Prints this message
    -v               Sets the level of verbosity
    -V, --version    Prints version information
OPTIONS:
    -c, --config <FILE>    Sets a custom config file
ARGS:
    INPUT    The input file to use
SUBCOMMANDS:
    help    Prints this message
    test    Controls testing features
```
**NOTE:** You could also run `myapp test --help` to see similar output and options for the
`test` subcommand.

- Compile the example `$ cargo build --release`
- Run the help info `$ ./target/release/claptests --help`
- Play with the arguments!

To test out `clap`’s default auto-generated help/version follow these steps:

- Create a new cargo project `$ cargo new fake --bin && cd fake`
- Add `clap`to your`Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
clap = "2"
```
- Add the following to your `src/main.rs`

```
extern crate clap;
use clap::App;
fn main() {
  App::new("fake").version("v1.0-beta").get_matches();
}
```
- Build your program `$ cargo build --release`
- Run with help or version `$ ./target/release/fake --help`or`$ ./target/release/fake --version`

For full usage, add `clap` as a dependency in your `Cargo.toml` (it is **highly** recommended to
use the `~major.minor.patch` style versions in your `Cargo.toml`, for more information see
[Compatibility Policy](https://docs.rs#compatibility-policy)) to use from crates.io:

```
[dependencies]
clap = "~2.27.0"
```
Or get the latest changes from the master branch at github:

```
[dependencies.clap]
git = "https://github.com/clap-rs/clap.git"
```
Add `extern crate clap;` to your crate root.

Define a list of valid arguments for your program (see the
[documentation](https://docs.rs/clap/) or [examples/](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/v2.34.0/examples) directory of this repo)

Then run `cargo build` or `cargo update && cargo build` for your project.

- `suggestions`: Turns on the- `Did you mean '--myoption'?`feature for when users make typos. (builds dependency- `strsim`)
- `color`: Turns on colored error messages. This feature only works on non-Windows OSs. (builds dependency- `ansi-term`and- `atty`)
- `wrap_help`: Wraps the help at the actual terminal width when available, instead of 120 characters. (builds dependency- `textwrap`with feature- `term_size`)

To disable these, add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies.clap]
version = "~2.27.0"
default-features = false
```
You can also selectively enable only the features you’d like to include, by adding:

```
[dependencies.clap]
version = "~2.27.0"
default-features = false
# Cherry-pick the features you'd like to use
features = [ "suggestions", "color" ]
```
- **“yaml”**: Enables building CLIs from YAML documents. (builds dependency- `yaml-rust`)
- **“unstable”**: Enables unstable- `clap`features that may change from release to release

The following graphic depicts `clap`s dependency graph (generated using
[cargo-graph](https://github.com/kbknapp/cargo-graph)).

- **Dashed**Line: Optional dependency
- **Red**Color:- **NOT**included by default (must use cargo- `features`to enable)
- **Blue**Color: Dev dependency, only used while developing.

From here on, I will list the appropriate `cargo` command as well as the `just` command.

Sometimes it’s helpful to only run a subset of the tests, which can be done via:

```
$ cargo test --test <test_name>
# Or
$ just run-test <test_name>
```
During the CI process `clap` runs against many different lints using
[ clippy](https://github.com/Manishearth/rust-clippy). In order to check if these lints pass on
your own computer prior to submitting a PR you’ll need a nightly compiler.

In order to check the code for lints run either:

```
$ rustup override add nightly
$ cargo build --features lints
$ rustup override remove
# Or
$ just lint
```
Another helpful technique is to see the `clap` debug output while developing features. In order
to see the debug output while running the full test suite or individual tests, run:

```
$ cargo test --features debug
# Or for individual tests
$ cargo test --test <test_name> --features debug
# The corresponding just command for individual debugging tests is:
$ just debug <test_name>
```
There are a few goals of `clap` that I’d like to maintain throughout contributions. If your
proposed changes break, or go against any of these goals we’ll discuss the changes further
before merging (but will *not* be ignored, all contributes are welcome!). These are by no means
hard-and-fast rules, as I’m no expert and break them myself from time to time (even if by
mistake or ignorance).

- Remain backwards compatible when possible
- If backwards compatibility *must*be broken, use deprecation warnings if at all possible before removing legacy code - This does not apply for security concerns

- If backwards compatibility
- Parse arguments quickly
- Parsing of arguments shouldn’t slow down usage of the main program - This is also true of
generating help and usage information (although *slightly*less stringent, as the program is about to exit)

- Parsing of arguments shouldn’t slow down usage of the main program - This is also true of
generating help and usage information (although
- Try to be cognizant of memory usage
- Once parsing is complete, the memory footprint of `clap`should be low since the main program is the star of the show

- Once parsing is complete, the memory footprint of
- `panic!`on- *developer*error, exit gracefully on- *end-user*error

Because `clap` takes `SemVer` and compatibility seriously, this is the official policy regarding
breaking changes and previous versions of Rust.

`clap` will pin the minimum required version of Rust to the CI builds. Bumping the minimum
version of Rust is considered a minor breaking change, meaning *at a minimum* the minor version
of `clap` will be bumped.

In order to keep from being surprised by breaking changes, it is **highly** recommended to use
the `~major.minor.patch` style in your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies] clap = "~2.27.0"
```
This will cause *only* the patch version to be updated upon a `cargo update` call, and therefore
cannot break due to new features, or bumped minimum versions of Rust.

`clap` will officially support current stable Rust, minus two releases, but may work with prior
releases as well. For example, current stable Rust at the time of this writing is 1.21.0,
meaning `clap` is guaranteed to compile with 1.19.0 and beyond. At the 1.22.0 release, `clap`
will be guaranteed to compile with 1.20.0 and beyond, etc.

Upon bumping the minimum version of Rust (assuming it’s within the stable-2 range), it *must* be
clearly annotated in the `CHANGELOG.md`

`clap` is licensed under the MIT license. Please read the [LICENSE-MIT](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v2.34.0/LICENSE-MIT) file in
this repository for more information.

- `pub use fmt::Format;`

- Counts the number of comma-delimited expressions passed to it. The result is a compile-time evaluable expression, suitable for use as a static array size, or the value of a`const`.
- Allows you to build the`App`instance from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- Build`App`,`Arg`s,`SubCommand`s and`Group`s with Usage-string like input but without the associated parsing runtime cost.
- Allows you to pull the authors for the app from your Cargo.toml at compile time in the form:`"author1 lastname <author1@example.com>:author2 lastname <author2@example.com>"`
- Allows you to pull the description from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- Allows you to pull the name from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- Allows you to pull the version from your Cargo.toml at compile time as`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH_PKGVERSION_PRE`
- A convenience macro for loading the YAML file at compile time (relative to the current file, like modules work). That YAML object can then be passed to this function.
- Convenience macro getting a typed value`T`where`T`implements`std::str::FromStr``Result<T,String>`which allows you as the developer to decide what you’d like to do on a failed parse. There are two types of errors, parse failures and those where the argument wasn’t present (such as a non-required argument). You can use it to get a single value, or a iterator as with the`ArgMatches::values_of`
- Convenience macro getting a typed value`Vec<T>``T`implements`std::str::FromStr``clap::Result<Vec<T>>`

- Used to create a representation of a command line program and all possible command line arguments. Application settings are set using the “builder pattern” with the`App::get_matches`
- The abstract representation of a command line argument. Used to set all the options and relationships that define a valid argument for the program.
- `ArgGroup`s are a family of related- [arguments](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)and way for you to express, “Any of these arguments”. By placing arguments in a logical group, you can create easier requirement and exclusion rules instead of having to list each argument individually, or when you want a rule to apply “any but not all” arguments.
- Command Line Argument Parser Error
- The abstract representation of a command line subcommand.

- Command line argument parser kind of error
- Describes which shell to produce a completions file for
